question:
A line passing through the points $A(1,2,3)$ and $B(5,8,11)$ intersects the line $\vec{r}=4\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda(5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$. Find the co-ordinates of the point of intersection.

Hence, write the equation of a line passing through the point of intersection and perpendicular to both the lines.
explanation:
Equation of line AB: $\vec{r} = \hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k} + \mu(4\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+8\hat{k})$
General point on AB: $(1+4\mu, 2+6\mu, 3+8\mu)$
General point on second line: $(4+5\lambda, 1+2\lambda, \lambda)$
For intersection, equate coordinates:
$1+4\mu = 4+5\lambda \implies 4\mu - 5\lambda = 3$
$2+6\mu = 1+2\lambda \implies 6\mu - 2\lambda = -1$
Solving these equations gives $\mu = -1/2, \lambda = -1$.
Checking the z-coordinate: $3+8(-1/2) = -1$ and $\lambda = -1$ (Matches).
Intersection point: $(-1, -1, -1)$.
Direction vector of perpendicular line: $\vec{d} = (4\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+8\hat{k}) \times (5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = -10\hat{i}+36\hat{j}-22\hat{k}$.
Equation of required line: $\vec{r} = -\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k} + t(-10\hat{i}+36\hat{j}-22\hat{k})$.
